CRL.M.A. 34778/2023 (Exemption)

3. The present application under Section 482 of the CrPC seeks following prayers;-
"It is, therefore, most respectfully prayed that petitioner no. 3 Saroj Devi may please be exempt to appear physically before this Hon'ble Court at the time of quashing petition in the interest of justice and in alternative, petitioner no. 3 will be appeared through VC, if required or directed by this Hon'ble Court.
Any other relief which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the facts and circumstances of the case."

5. Learned APP for the State and learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent no. 2 accepts notice and fairly do not oppose the present application.
6.
In view of the averments made in the application, the same is allowed and dispose of accordingly.

7. Petitioner no. 3 is exempted from personal appearance and permitted to appear through video conferencing.
8.

The present petition filed under Section 482 of the CrPC seeks quashing of the FIR No. 24/2022,
under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Burari and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms.
Reetika Jain, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

sentences.text: 9. The marriage between petitioner no.1/husband and respondent no.2/wife was solemnized on 15.01.2016 as per Hindu rites and ceremonies.
10. No child was born out of the said wedlock.
11. Due to matrimonial differences between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2, the parties started residing separately from 18.12.2018.

Subsequently, respondent no.2/complainant lodged an FIR against petitioner no.1 (husband), petitioner no. 2 (father-in-law), petitioner no. 3 (mother-in- law)
and petitioner no. 4 (brother-in-law).
12.

On 17.11.2023, parties arrived at a settlement before the learned Metropolitan Magistrate and as per the said settlement deed, petitioner no.1 has agreed to pay an amount of Rs. 8,50,000/- to the respondent no.2/wife
This is a digitally signed order.

The copy of the order of aforesaid settlement dated 17.11.2023 is on record (Annexure P- 2).

13. In terms of the said settlement, the marriage between the parties stands dissolved by a decree of divorce dated 14.02.2022, passed by learned Principal Judge, Family Court Kangra at Dharamshala (Annexure P-6).

sentences.text: Petitioners 1, 2 and 4 and complainant/respondent no. 2 are present before the Court and petitioner no. 3 is present through video conferencing and have been duly identified by their respective counsel, as well as the Investigating Officer, SI Rajeev, PS Burari.

15. A demand draft bearing no. 944494 dated 29.11.2023 for Rs. 8,50,000/- drawn on Axis Bank,
Shimla, Himachal Pradesh, has been handed over complainant/Respondent No.2, who acknowledges the receipt of the same.
16. The complainant/respondent No.2 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners and she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She further states that all the terms of the agreement have been complied with.
17. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.

18. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes by observing as under:-

... In other words, the High Court must consider whether it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceedings or continuation of criminal proceedings would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

19. In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 24/2022, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Burari and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms. Reetika Jain,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi.

20. In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 24/2022, under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC, registered at P.S. Burari and all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom, including the chargesheet pending before the court of Ms. Reetika Jain,
learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Mahila Court, Tis Hazari Courts, Delhi, is hereby quashed.
